subject: Post-call: open vs baseline trial scope and acceptance thresholds
messages:
From: Samantha Reed <samantha@finmetrics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, Feb 25, 2027 at 4:10 PM -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: discovery + next steps

Thanks for the call earlier today — good discussion. Quick recap and a couple of asks from our side so we can scope the trial: 

- Primary goal: reliable customer support summarization and routing (short form summaries + intent extraction).
- Current baseline: internal proprietary model (v2) used by our support automation. Main concerns: hallucination on policy questions, and cost at 10k daily requests.
- What we need from Redwood to evaluate:
  1) a short comparison (latency, token cost, observed F1 on our sample intents) between your recommended open models vs our baseline;
  2) a 2-week trial plan (pilot traffic guidance, canary thresholds);
  3) the prompt bundle and sample benchmark set you’ll run against.

Can you send the trial scope + acceptance criteria (we want to avoid regressions), plus any compliance evidence (SOC2 summary) for procurement?

Thanks — I can loop in our procurement lead once we have a quote and SOC2 summary.

Samantha
Samantha Reed
Head of AI Ops, FinMetrics
Samantha@finmetrics.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha@finmetrics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, Feb 25, 2027 at 6:25 PM -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: discovery + next steps (open vs baseline trial plan)

Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and for walking us through the baseline behavior. High level response and next steps below; attached the prompt bundle and a short benchmark summary to start.

High-level recommendations
- Trial targets: run a 2-week blind trial with 10k daily requests mirrored from a 10% sample of traffic. Start with two open models we recommend (OpenFast-1.3Q and Clarion-1.0-int8) and Redwood’s baseline-compat variant for quick fallback to the proprietary baseline if needed.
- Acceptance thresholds (proposal):
  * Intent extraction F1 >= baseline F1 - 0.03 (allow small gap),
  * Summarization ROUGE-L >= baseline - 0.05,
  * Hallucination rate (policy Qs) <= baseline + 0.02 (we'll instrument a small manual check set),
  * 95th pct latency < 400ms for requests <= 512 tokens,
  * Cost per 1k tokens not to exceed 0.9x current unit in pilot (we'll show expected spend).

Risk controls and measurement
- We'll run parallel scoring on your labeled test set (please share) and an interleaved human review set for the first 500 policy-sensitive responses.
- Canary policy: 1% mirrored -> 5% -> 10% (auto-stop if hallucination or severe drop detected).
- Regression alarms: nightly checks against the prompt bundle; automated rollback to baseline variant on breach.

Attachments included
- prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts + annotations),
- benchmark-results-summary.pdf (preliminary micro-benchmarks showing token throughput & latency),
- redwood-trial-quote.xlsx (preliminary pricing for 2-week pilot).

Related links
- HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/contacts/12345
- Eval dashboard (read-only): https://dash.redwood.ai/evals/finmetrics/2027-02-26
- Drive: https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c

Next steps / asks from FinMetrics
1) Share your labeled intent/summary test set (even small, 200–500 rows) so we can compute parity metrics.
2) Confirm a preferred start date for the 2-week trial window.
3) Procurement: send SOC2 summary or procurement contact and we’ll forward our compliance pack and quote.

I’ll schedule a 30-min checkpoint mid-pilot to review metrics; Marissa/ Priyom — looping you for procurement & pricing next steps.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, Feb 26, 2027 at 9:15 AM -08:00
Subject: Internal: FinMetrics pilot — procurement & contract readiness

Internal notes (Marissa) — keeping this short: 
- Deal health: good interest, they stressed parity and tight hallucination tolerance. Likely to convert if trial shows parity on intent and lower cost.
- Pricing: the attached quote is conservative. Priyom, can you prepare an accelerated pilot discount (one-time credit) we can offer for a 2-week proof of value? Suggest 40% off list for the pilot.
- Compliance: Samantha asked for SOC2 summary. I attached the standard SOC2 summary doc link to reply with; procurement will ask for data retention and export controls as well.
- Ops: we should propose the canary thresholds Marcus suggested and offer a Redwood-hosted audit log view for their SREs.

Action items for Priyom:
1) Draft a short pilot amendment (2-week trial, mirror 10% traffic, cost cap).
2) Prepare discount line and payment terms to include when we loop procurement.
3) Collect SOC2 summary + data flow diagram for reply.

Marissa
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Samantha Reed <samantha@finmetrics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, FinMetrics Procurement <procurement@finmetrics.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 26, 2027 at 11:02 AM -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: open vs baseline trial plan

Thanks Marcus — the attachments and the acceptance thresholds are helpful. A few clarifying questions before we share the labeled set: 

1) For the intent F1 threshold you proposed (baseline - 0.03), can you provide a short table that shows expected F1 for the two open models vs our baseline on a 200-sample snapshot? If possible include confidence intervals.
2) The hallucination metric — how will Redwood define and measure "policy hallucination" in the pilot? We need a definition prior to starting.
3) Procurement asked to see the SOC2 summary (I’ve cc’d procurement). Please attach the SOC2 summary and the data retention policy.

If you can get the table and SOC2 over by EOD Monday (our time), we can get procurement to review and set up the trial kickoff for Wed next week.

Samantha

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha@finmetrics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, FinMetrics Procurement <procurement@finmetrics.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 27, 2027 at 9:45 AM -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: open vs baseline trial plan — deliverables + timeline

Samantha — attaching the short comparison table you asked for and the SOC2 summary link in the Drive (see links below). Quick notes: 

- Snapshot results (200-sample, 95% CI):
  * Open model OpenFast-1.3Q — Intent F1: 0.82 (±0.03), Summarization ROUGE-L: 0.60 (±0.04)
  * Open model Clarion-1.0-int8 — Intent F1: 0.79 (±0.04), Summarization ROUGE-L: 0.58 (±0.05)
  * FinMetrics baseline (v2) — Intent F1: 0.84 (±0.03), Summarization ROUGE-L: 0.63 (±0.03)

- Interpretation: both open candidates come within the proposed intent gap; Clarion shows slightly higher variance on small test sets. That said, the hallucination metric is use-case specific — we define "policy hallucination" as any generated assertion contradicting a policy excerpt in the test set or an invented policy reference. For the pilot we will flag these via an automated heuristic and then confirm via human review on the 500-sample policy set.

- SOC2 and compliance: SOC2 summary uploaded to Drive: https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c (file: SOC2-summary-redwood-2026.pdf). Procurement: please confirm whom we should send the full compliance pack and an IP/data processing addendum.

Proposed timeline:
- Mon (EOD FinMetrics): FinMetrics provides 200-sample labeled snapshot + procurement contact.
- Tue: Redwood runs the snapshot, returns the full comparison table and a pilot amendment draft.
- Wed: Kickoff pilot (mirror 10% initial -> expand per canary).

Marissa / Priyom — if you’re good with the 40% pilot credit we discussed I’ll include that in the amendment and send to procurement.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot started.

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
